title: The Farmer Who Waded Through Muddy, Rat-Infested Water — Suspected Leptospirosis on Top of Diabetes

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 60 years old, an agile farmer whose work involves tilling land and working barefoot in muddy waters infested with rats. He presents with a week-long history of malaise, diffuse muscle aches, abdominal distension, loss of appetite, and increased urine output.

He had been well until a week before this, when he developed fever with loss of appetite. The fever was low-grade, with a mild evening rise. He saw a doctor who prescribed symptomatic treatment that brought quick relief, but his appetite loss persisted, and for the last four days he has had fatigue and muscle aches. He denies unintentional weight loss, vomiting, changes in bowel habits, jaundice, or altered taste.

He has chronic diabetes and hypertension, managed with telmisartan plus hydrochlorothiazide, along with glibenclamide and metformin, though his adherence to salt and sugar restriction has been poor; he otherwise eats a fairly balanced diet. He reports unrefreshing sleep for several years, and his wife notes that he snores, though he has no daytime sleepiness. He occasionally gets up at night to urinate but denies nighttime diarrhea, urinary frequency, urgency, or hesitancy.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **Vitals:** pulse 93 bpm, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, temperature 98.3°F, respiratory rate 22/min, oxygen saturation 97% on room air; random blood sugar markedly elevated at 664 mg/dL
- **General exam:** tiny bilateral subconjunctival hemorrhages with marked conjunctival suffusion and icterus; moist tongue and mucous membranes; Mallampati class 3 airway; Terry's nails noted; no cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy; bilateral pitting pedal edema with pits resolving in about 40 seconds
- **Abdominal exam:** distended, with a central, inverted umbilicus and no visible dilated veins or pulsations; soft and non-tender on palpation with no organomegaly; bowel sounds present; no specific tender points on muscle examination
- **Systemic exam:** bilateral air entry with no added sounds; heart sounds normal without murmurs; no focal neurological deficit
- **Liver function:** total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 2.5 mg/dL, ALP 550 IU/L, total protein 5.9 g/dL, albumin low at 2.9 g/dL
- **Renal function and electrolytes:** blood urea markedly elevated at 150 mg/dL, serum creatinine 3.5 mg/dL, sodium 129 mEq/L (low), potassium 4.3 mEq/L, chloride 90 mEq/L (low)
- **Urinalysis:** 8–10 pus cells noted, without acidosis or ketones on further metabolic work-up

**Working diagnosis:** Given his occupational exposure to muddy, rodent-infested water, his conjunctival suffusion and hemorrhages, jaundice, and acute kidney injury, leptospirosis was suspected as the primary diagnosis, layered onto diabetic nephropathy with hypoalbuminemia (in the setting of 10 years of diabetes) and hypertension. His hyponatremia and hypochloremia were attributed to either an underlying interstitial nephritis (suggested by the pus cells in his urine) or to his long-term thiazide diuretic use.

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He was started on aspirin-atorvastatin combination therapy, continued telmisartan for his hypertension, IV thiamine and B-complex supplementation, and metformin for glycemic control, with blood pressure, temperature, pulse, and glucose monitored every four hours while the leptospirosis work-up and management of his acute kidney injury proceeded.
